points: **Osler nodes:** traditionally **immunological** (immune-complex vasculitis); histology also shows microemboli. They count as an **immunological phenomenon** in the Duke criteria.
**Janeway lesions:** **septic microemboli** with dermal microabscesses (a **vascular phenomenon**), so organisms may be cultured from them.
**Splinters:** rupture of longitudinally oriented nail-bed capillaries (trauma) or microemboli/vasculitis.
≥3 sets of blood cultures **before antibiotics**, echocardiography (TTE → TOE), FBC, CRP, urinalysis.

cards.name: Osler nodes
cards.clue: SLE, **gonococcaemia**, typhoid, haemolytic anaemia, marantic (non-bacterial thrombotic) endocarditis, infected radial-artery lines (distal emboli), vasculitis

cards.name: Janeway lesions
cards.clue: SLE, gonococcaemia, typhoid, other septicaemia, haemolytic anaemia

cards.name: Splinter haemorrhages
cards.clue: **Trauma (commonest — manual workers, distal splinters)**, **psoriasis**, **onychomycosis**, eczema, haemodialysis, vasculitis/connective tissue disease, **antiphospholipid syndrome**, trichinosis, high altitude, mitral stenosis, scurvy, drugs (tetracyclines, VEGF-inhibitors such as sunitinib/sorafenib), and some normal elderly people

items.t: Fever with a new murmur, splinters or Osler/Janeway lesions: **same-day admission**; do not give antibiotics before blood cultures unless septic.
